title: 10/31 시험 기출
intro: 2026년 10월 31일 실제 시험(난이도 4)에 나온 주제 묶음입니다: 자기소개 · 서점(particular 책) · 골프 · 새로운 이웃 · 기념 휴일. 주제는 실제 기출이고, 질문 문장은 그 주제로 자주 나오는 형태로 만든 예상 질문입니다. 모범답안의 '나'는 이날 서베이에 맞춰 '분당 아파트에 혼자 살고, 지금은 일을 하지 않음, 여가: 독서 · 골프 · 조깅 · 카페 · 영화 · TV'로 통일했습니다. 서베이를 이번과 같게 고르면 이 답안을 그대로 쓸 수 있어요.
strategy: 자기소개에서 말한 소재(혼자 사는 집 · 서현역 서점 · 골프 연습장 · 탄천 조깅)를 다른 문제에서 그대로 다시 쓰세요.
서점 · 골프는 설문 주제라 묘사 → 루틴 → 경험 콤보로 나옵니다. 경험 질문은 반드시 과거시제로 말하세요.
새로운 이웃 · 기념 휴일은 돌발 주제로 나왔습니다. 옆집 박 할머니, 위층 새 부부, 대전 부모님 댁 추석처럼 이야기 하나씩을 정해 두면 당황하지 않아요.
난이도 4는 IM2~IH를 노리는 구간입니다. IM3 답안을 먼저 입에 붙이고, 여유가 생기면 IH 디테일을 한두 문장씩 더하세요.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about myself. I live alone in a small apartment in Bundang, near Seoul. I'm not working at the moment, so I have a lot of free time. I'm a calm person, and I like quiet places. In my free time, I read books, go jogging, and play golf. On weekends, I often go to a bookstore or a cafe near my place. Living alone is really comfortable, and I enjoy my own time. Yeah, that's a little bit about me.
answers.IH: Okay, let me tell you a little bit about myself. I live alone in a small apartment in Bundang, which is just south of Seoul. I'm not working at the moment, so my days are pretty flexible. I'd describe myself as a calm and curious person. I don't like crowded places, but I love learning new things. That's why I spend a lot of time reading, especially at a big bookstore near Seohyeon Station. To stay healthy, I go jogging along the Tancheon stream a few times a week. I also got into golf a couple of years ago, and now I practice at a driving range near my place. In the evenings, I usually watch TV or listen to music at home. Living alone can be a little quiet sometimes, but I really enjoy having my own space. Yeah, that's a little bit about me.
answers.AL: Okay, let me tell you a little bit about myself. I live on my own in a cozy apartment in Bundang, a quiet area just south of Seoul. I'm not working at the moment, so I have a lot of control over my schedule, which I really appreciate. If I had to describe myself in a few words, I'd say I'm calm, curious, and a bit of a homebody. I'm not really into crowded places, but I never get tired of learning something new. So a typical day for me starts with a jog along the Tancheon stream, where the air is fresh in the morning. After that, I often head to a big bookstore near Seohyeon Station and lose track of time browsing new books. A couple of years ago, I also picked up golf, and honestly, it has become a bit of an obsession. I hit balls at a driving range near my place, and once in a while, I play a real round with my friends. In the evenings, I just relax at home with some music or a TV show. Living alone can feel a little quiet at times, but I've come to love the freedom of having my own space. I think this lifestyle really suits me right now. Yeah, that's pretty much who I am.

questions.en: What do you usually do when you go to a bookstore? Describe a typical visit from beginning to end.
questions.ko: 서점에 가면 보통 무엇을 하나요? 처음부터 끝까지 평소 방문 과정을 설명해 주세요.
tips: 10/31 기출 주제: 서점. 루틴 질문은 First → Then → After that → Before I leave 순서 연결어로 이어 가세요.
usually · always · sometimes 같은 빈도 부사를 꼭 넣으세요.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you what I usually do at the bookstore. I usually go there on weekday afternoons because it's not crowded. First, I check the bestseller section near the entrance. Then, I go to the novel section and look around for a while. If I find an interesting book, I sit at the big table and read a few pages. After that, I usually buy one or two books. Sometimes I also buy a coffee at the cafe inside. I usually stay there for about two hours. Yeah, that's what I usually do at the bookstore.
answers.IH: Okay, let me walk you through a typical visit to the bookstore. Since I'm not working right now, I usually go there on weekday afternoons when it's nice and quiet. The first thing I do is check the bestseller list near the entrance to see what people are reading these days. After that, I head straight to the fiction section, because I'm a big fan of mystery novels. When a book catches my eye, I take it to the big wooden table and read the first chapter. If it hooks me, I buy it, and if not, I just put it back and keep looking. I also like to stop by the stationery corner and look at notebooks and pens, even though I don't really need them. Before I leave, I usually grab an iced americano at the cafe inside. All in all, I end up staying there for two or three hours without even noticing. Yeah, that's how a typical visit goes for me.
answers.AL: Okay, let me walk you through what a typical bookstore visit looks like for me. Since I'm not working at the moment, I usually go on a weekday afternoon, when the place is quiet and I can actually find a seat. I always start at the bestseller display by the entrance, just to get a sense of what people are into these days. Then I make my way to the fiction section, because I'm a sucker for mystery novels. My rule is pretty simple: if a book catches my eye, I read the first chapter at the big wooden table before deciding. If the story grabs me, I buy it right away, but if it doesn't, I put it back without any guilt. Along the way, I usually wander into the stationery corner and end up buying a notebook I definitely don't need. Before heading home, I treat myself to an iced americano at the little cafe inside and flip through my new book. Before I know it, two or three hours have flown by. For me, it's not just shopping, it's more like a small ritual that recharges me. Yeah, that's pretty much how my bookstore visits go.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about my golf routine. I go to the driving range about three times a week. I usually go in the morning because it's not busy. First, I stretch for about five minutes. Then, I hit about two hundred balls for an hour. I start with short clubs and finish with the driver. After practice, I check my swing videos on my phone. Then I go home and take a shower. Yeah, that's my usual golf routine.
answers.IH: Okay, let me walk you through my golf routine. I go to the driving range about three times a week, usually in the morning when it's quiet. Before I start, I always stretch my shoulders and back for about five minutes, because I hurt my back once. Then I warm up with short wedge shots and slowly move up to the longer irons. I always save the driver for last, since that's the most fun part. In total, I hit around two hundred balls in an hour. While I practice, I record my swing on my phone so I can check what I'm doing wrong. After that, I often go to the putting green and practice short putts for about twenty minutes. When I get home, I watch my swing videos and compare them with golf lessons on YouTube. Yeah, that's pretty much my golf routine.
answers.AL: Okay, let me walk you through my golf routine, because I'm actually pretty strict about it. I hit the driving range about three times a week, usually first thing in the morning, when it's nice and empty. Before I even touch a club, I spend about five minutes stretching my shoulders and lower back, since I strained my back once and learned my lesson. Then I warm up with short wedge shots and gradually work my way up to the longer irons. I always save the driver for last, because, let's be honest, smashing the ball as far as I can is the most satisfying part. All in all, I go through around two hundred balls in about an hour. While I'm practicing, I set up my phone on a little tripod and record my swing from the side. Once I'm done with full swings, I head over to the putting green and spend another twenty minutes on short putts, which is where most of my strokes are wasted. Later at home, I go over the videos and compare my swing with lessons on YouTube. It might sound a bit obsessive, but seeing even a small improvement makes it all worth it. Yeah, that's pretty much my golf routine.

On Chuseok, people make songpyeon and visit their ancestors' graves. There are also other holidays like Children's Day and Christmas. Yeah, those are the main holidays in Korea.

On Seollal morning, people wear hanbok, eat rice cake soup, and bow deeply to their parents. In return, the elders give money to the kids, so children love this holiday. On Chuseok, families make half-moon shaped rice cakes called songpyeon and visit their ancestors' graves. answers.AL: Okay, let me tell you about holidays in Korea. The two biggest ones by far are Seollal, which is the Lunar New Year, and Chuseok, which is often described as Korean Thanksgiving. During these holidays, millions of people head back to their hometowns at the same time, so the highways basically turn into giant parking lots. On Seollal morning, people dress up in hanbok, eat a bowl of rice cake soup, and perform a deep bow to their elders. In return, the elders hand out envelopes of money along with words of wisdom, which is why kids look forward to it all year. Chuseok, on the other hand, is a harvest festival, so families make half-moon shaped rice cakes called songpyeon and pay respects at their ancestors' graves. Interestingly, these days more and more people take advantage of long holidays to travel abroad rather than stick to the old traditions. Personally, since I live alone, I see the holidays as a precious chance to reconnect with my family. Yeah, that's a quick overview of holidays in Korea.
